home.infotitle: Why is it important to know the public information of your website?
home.paragraph1: As human rights defenders, journalists, and activists, it is essential that we take steps to protect our digital platforms. The public information of your website, such as metadata or exposed security settings, can be used by malicious actors to compromise your security or that of your community.
home.paragraph2: "Veni OSINT" is a tool designed to help you easily visualize this public information and provide a clear overview of potential risks. By knowing what data is accessible, you can take informed actions to improve your website's security and strengthen your digital protection.
home.paragraph3: This tool is aimed at those fighting for a more just and secure world, providing them with the control and knowledge necessary to keep their digital work safe.
home.lead: See what public information your website exposes: DNS, certificates, headers, ports and more.
home.subLead: Type your site's address and in under a minute you will get an overview of its configuration and possible weak spots.
home.inputHint: You can enter a domain, a URL or an IP address.
home.privacyHint: No analytics, no cookies. Some checks query external services.

items.ssllabs: Analyzes the server's SSL/TLS configuration and grades it.
items.virustotal: Checks the domain against dozens of antivirus engines.
items.shodan: Search engine for internet-connected devices and services.
items.archive: Previous versions of the site saved by the Internet Archive.
items.urlscan: Scans a URL and shows which resources the page connects to.
items.sucuri: Looks for known malware and blacklisting.
items.nslookup: Shows all DNS records for the domain.
items.dnschecker: Checks DNS propagation across servers worldwide.
items.censys: Hosts and certificates associated with the domain.
items.pagespeed: Performance, accessibility and SEO on mobile and desktop.
items.builtwith: Technologies the site is built with.
items.dnsdumpster: Maps a domain from its DNS records.
items.internetnl: Checks for modern standards: IPv6, DNSSEC, HTTPS and more.
items.securityheaders: Grades the site's HTTP security headers.
items.radar: Domain ranking and traffic data from Cloudflare.

about.privacyDescription: Veni OSINT uses no analytics, cookies or third-party error logging. We don't store the addresses you scan. As with any website, our hosting provider (Netlify) may temporarily log technical request data.
about.title: About Veni OSINT
about.privacyThirdParties: To get some results, our server queries external services (such as Google DNS, the Internet Archive, Tranco, ipwho.is or block lists), which receive the scanned domain or IP. Your browser only connects to veni.chequea.la.

threats.title: The site is reported as dangerous
threats.desc: Security services flag it for phishing or malware. Browsers may warn visitors.
threats.action: Write to us as soon as possible: it usually means the site was compromised.

blocklisted.title: The domain is blocked by: {{lists}}
blocklisted.desc: Some networks and DNS filters prevent people from reaching your site.
blocklisted.action: Check the site for malware, then request a review from each list. We can help.

domainExpiry.title: The domain expires in {{days}} days
domainExpiry.desc: If it expires, the site and email stop working and someone else could register it.
domainExpiry.action: Renew it with your registrar and turn on auto-renewal.

sslExpired.title: The HTTPS certificate has expired
sslExpired.desc: Browsers show a "not secure" warning and many people won't be able to get in.
sslExpired.action: Renew the certificate from your hosting (e.g. with Let's Encrypt, which is free).

sslExpiring.title: The HTTPS certificate expires in {{days}} days
sslExpiring.desc: When it expires, browsers will show a "not secure" warning.
sslExpiring.action: Make sure your hosting renews it automatically.

wpUsers.title: WordPress shows the admin users: {{users}}
wpUsers.desc: Anyone can see the usernames used to log in, which makes password-guessing attacks easier.
wpUsers.action: Block the REST API user list (e.g. with a security plugin), use long passwords and turn on two-factor authentication.

wpXmlrpc.title: xmlrpc.php is enabled
wpXmlrpc.desc: It is an old WordPress entry point widely used to try passwords at scale.
wpXmlrpc.action: Disable it if you don't use the WordPress mobile app or Jetpack.

wpVersion.title: The WordPress version is visible ({{version}})
wpVersion.desc: It helps anyone looking for sites running vulnerable versions.
wpVersion.action: Keep WordPress updated and hide the version from the site's code.

criticalPorts.title: Sensitive services open to the internet (ports {{ports}})
criticalPorts.desc: These are databases or remote desktops: they should not be reachable from anywhere.
criticalPorts.action: Ask your hosting to close them or allow only known addresses.

openPorts.title: Open ports besides the web: {{ports}}
openPorts.desc: Every open service is one more door that has to be kept up to date.
openPorts.action: Check with your hosting whether you need them; close the ones you don't use.

noDmarc.title: The domain has no DMARC for email
noDmarc.desc: Without DMARC it is easy to send fake emails pretending to be your organization, for example for phishing.
noDmarc.action: Add a TXT record at _dmarc.yourdomain. If you don't send email from the domain, use "v=DMARC1; p=reject".

noSpf.title: The domain has no SPF for email
noSpf.desc: SPF says which servers may send email on your behalf.
noSpf.action: Add a "v=spf1 ..." TXT record from your email provider, or "v=spf1 -all" if you don't send email.

noHsts.title: The site doesn't enforce HTTPS (no HSTS)
noHsts.desc: A connection could be downgraded to the unencrypted version of the site, e.g. on public wifi.
noHsts.action: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header on your server or hosting.

headers.title: Missing security headers: {{headers}}
headers.desc: They help the browser block attacks like clickjacking or code injection.
headers.action: Add them in your server or hosting configuration. The Check List explains how.

noDnssec.title: The domain doesn't use DNSSEC
noDnssec.desc: DNSSEC prevents forged DNS answers that send people to another site.
noDnssec.action: Turn it on at your registrar or DNS provider; many do it with one click.

noSecurityTxt.title: No security.txt
noSecurityTxt.desc: A file that tells people whom to contact if they find a security problem on your site.

exposedFiles.title: Sensitive files are publicly visible: {{paths}}
exposedFiles.desc: They may contain passwords, the site source code or database copies, and anyone can download them.
exposedFiles.action: Delete them from the server or block access as soon as possible, and change any passwords they contain. Write to us if you need help.

exposedInfo.title: Technical information is visible: {{paths}}
exposedInfo.desc: It shows server configuration details or the file list of a folder.
exposedInfo.action: Remove those pages or turn off directory listing on your server.

danglingCname.title: Subdomain pointing to a service that no longer exists: {{names}}
danglingCname.desc: It points (CNAME) to a service that no longer exists. Someone could create that service and publish anything on your subdomain.
danglingCname.action: Delete that CNAME record at your DNS provider if you no longer use it.

exposedFiles.none: No sensitive files found exposed ({{count}} checked).
exposedFiles.note: For safety, veni never shows the contents of these files.
